species: The human remains found in the bog of Vittrup include a right ankle bone (talus), the shaft of a lower left shin bone (tibia), a fragmented skull and a jawbone (mandibula)
tissue: Palaeoproteomic analysis of dental calculus can be informative for subsistence studies
disease_state: The outer surface of the cranial vault, more specifically on the top of the head, on the forehead and on the back of the head displays small diffused porosities with rounded margins, characteristic of porotic hyperostosis.
sample_source: We, therefore, present the remains as a single individual: Vittrup Man.
age: we judge 30–40 years to be a reasonable estimate and consider the low end of this range the most likely.
sex: the skull and lower jawbone are determined to be of a male.
